plates.side_label: IMMUNE CELLS SHUFFLE THEIR OWN DNA
plates.quality_reason: Quality: readable faces (37-year-old Japanese molecular biologist Susumu Tonegawa and postdoctoral fellow Nobumichi Hozumi at the Basel Institute for Immunology in October 1976 comparing embryo DNA and adult B-cell DNA with restriction enzymes to prove somatic V(D)J recombination).
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Split period scene: on the left at the Basel Institute for Immunology in October 1976, Susumu Tonegawa and Nobumichi Hozumi examine restriction-enzyme DNA hybridization plots; on the right, a chromosome diagram shows widely separated embryonic V, D, and J gene segments being cut and spliced together in an adult B-cell. No readable words or numbers anywhere. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer. No Orbit.

teach_overlay.label: Immune cells shuffle their own DNA
teach_overlay.timeline_step: 3/3 · Oct 1976 (Susumu Tonegawa & Nobumichi Hozumi in Basel prove somatic V(D)J DNA recombination generates >10 billion antibodies from modular gene segments, winning the 1987 Nobel Prize)

plates.side_label: OCT 1976 HOZUMI & TONEGAWA (PNAS 73: 3628–3632): EMBRYO SEPARATED V–C DNA FRAGMENTS VS SPLICED B-CELL V(D)J GENE (40 V × 23 D × 6 J × LIGHT CHAIN × JUNCTIONS > 10^10)
plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Hozumi & Tonegawa (October 1976, PNAS 73: 3628–3632) somatic V(D)J recombination chart shows embryonic germline DNA (widely separated V, D, J, and C gene segments on different restriction fragments) vs rearranged adult B-cell DNA (1 V + 1 D + 1 J spliced together next to C), multiplying ~40 VH x 23 DH x 6 JH x light-chain Vk/l-Jk/l x junctional additions into >10^10 unique antibodies.

teach_overlay.detail: Inked Hozumi & Tonegawa (October 1976, PNAS 73: 3628–3632) somatic V(D)J recombination chart on period paper showing embryonic germline DNA (widely separated V, D, J, and C gene segments on different restriction fragments) vs rearranged adult B-cell DNA (1 V + 1 D + 1 J spliced together next to C), multiplying ~40 VH × 23 DH × 6 JH × light-chain Vκ/λ-Jκ/λ × junctional additions into >10^10 unique antibodies
teach_overlay.scale: with just three modularity reels — V, D, and J — plus random letters inserted at the joints, your DNA works like a combination lock where a few dozen dials can dial up ten billion different numbers
